title: Frigate
description: Live video from your Frigate cameras: one camera full size, or several in a grid, with what each one detected. Optionally on an old CRT security monitor.

setup.intro: Shows your Frigate cameras live, with what each one detected recently.

steps: Copy the address you open Frigate at, such as https://frigate.local:8971/ at home or https://cameras.example.com/ from outside. Include a path if your proxy serves Frigate under one.
Use a Frigate user’s name and password. An admin can add one in Frigate under Settings → Users; the viewer role is enough.

Frigate’s own certificate on port 8971 is self-signed, and Dashledge accepts only one this Mac trusts. Give Frigate a trusted certificate (see Frigate’s TLS guide), or open the certificate in Keychain Access and set it to Always Trust.
Use Frigate’s internal port 5000, such as http://frigate.local:5000/. It needs no sign-in, so use it only on a network you trust.
If port 5000 doesn’t answer, check that your Frigate container publishes it (ports: "5000:5000" in Docker Compose).
